question: Should workflow-style session completion automation be supported through a new internal `session:end` hook, or should maintainers designate typed plugin `session_end` as the supported surface instead?
rationale: Current main has a plugin lifecycle hook but no internal hook event, and VISION.md pushes optional capabilities toward plugins unless an extension API gap needs core design work.

options.title: Add internal `session:end`
options.body: Implement and document a typed internal hook event across the relevant completion paths so operator-installed `HOOK.md` automation can react directly.

options.title: Use plugin `session_end` only
options.body: Document typed plugin `session_end` as the supported workflow integration surface and close or narrow the internal-hook request accordingly.

options.title: Limit to reset-hook PR
options.body: Treat the open reset-hook PR as a separate partial fix for daily/idle memory behavior while leaving this broader API decision unresolved.

recommendation.title: Add internal `session:end`
recommendation.body: Implement and document a typed internal hook event across the relevant completion paths so operator-installed `HOOK.md` automation can react directly.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision hinges on the plugin hook contract boundary versus internal hook surface, and recent plugin hook contract work points to this owner as the best routing candidate.
